why: NumPy Agent.infer_policies calls this on every decision. It loops policies in Python and, for each one, softmaxes the same preference vector and rescores state information gain. Those likelihood entropies and the preference normalization do not depend on the policy, so hoisting them should cut a large share of the ~835 ms without changing q_pi. Open PRs only touch the separate _full policy updaters; spm_MDP_G itself is already optimized and is not the target.

Exhaustive JAX policy posterior with utility, state information gain, and parameter information gain (1728 policies, horizon 3). Compiled parameter scoring on this same model is several times the state-and-utility path because spm_wnorm of pA/pB and the entropy of A are recomputed inside every policy step even though they depend only on the generative model. Computing those weights once per call should remove most of that gap. The inductive sibling is what Agent.infer_policies uses and is left out because issue 166 proposes changing it; this entry point is not in an open PR.

Public constructor for the exhaustive policy matrix (5 actions, horizon 6, 15625 policies). It builds a nested Python tuple per policy and then walks that object tree into one array. Filling a single integer array in itertools order returns the same matrix and drops the tuple round-trip, which is most of the ~59 ms.

Sequence variational free energy on a 4096-step trajectory, including observation accuracy, transition cross-entropy, and Dirichlet parameter KL. The scan recomputes log-likelihood and log-transition contractions from the raw A and B tensors at every timestep. log(A) is constant along the trajectory and log(B) depends on time only through the action index, so hoisting those logs preserves the scalar free energy and should remove a substantial fraction of the ~19 ms. Not touched by the open infer_states optimization PR.
